name: B10-0048/2024 (ECR) – The deteriorating situation of women in Afghanistan due to the recent adoption of the law on the ‘Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice’
title: Resolution on the deteriorating situation of women in Afghanistan due to the recent adoption of the law on the “Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice”
part_text:
The European Parliament strongly condemns a new Taliban law that it says wipes women out of public life and violates their basic human rights. It asks the United Nations Human Rights Council to set up an inquiry into Taliban abuses, and the International Criminal Court to investigate the Taliban's Supreme Council. It also calls for sanctions to be enforced against Taliban leaders, for the law to be abolished, and for a new European Union envoy on freedom of religion. The text is a statement of position; it does not itself change any law.

- The Taliban face calls for sanctions, travel bans and asset freezes; Afghan women and girls are most affected.
- The United Nations Human Rights Council and the International Criminal Court are asked to investigate Taliban leaders.
- The European Commission is asked to appoint a new envoy on freedom of religion; no date is set.
